checks: No eclipse at 1 of 15 covered epochs where the 3.10423 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: TIC 468090770 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 3.104225 days, identified through automated analysis of TESS photometry. The primary eclipse produces a 2.17% dimming of the star's light, while no secondary eclipse was detected. The transit signal shows high statistical significance with a BLS detection value of 174.1 and pixel-level confirmation at a signal-to-noise ratio of 31.7, though the source appears offset by 4.7 arcsec in the difference imaging. This candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs. However, alternating eclipses show significantly different depths - a pattern suggesting the actual orbital period may be twice the initially measured value. While pixel-level confirmation and eclipse timing remain unaffected by this issue, the depth variations indicate some open questions about the system's true nature that warrant further investigation.
